title: starter-wizard-handbook-mini-lab-sketch
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for a compact, interactive 'Starter Wizard' that guides a new developer from zero to a running sample app in ~10 minutes. Goal is to reduce first-run friction, capture high-signal telemetry opt-ins, and provide a reproducible local lab environment for SDK experiments.

Audience:
- New SDK adopters (engineers, ML engineers)
- Developer advocates running workshops
- Internal bootstrappers for demos

Constraints / guiding principles:
- Do not require account sign-in for the local lab (allow mock keys), but clearly show production onboarding next steps.
- Keep CLI surface < 6 commands for the happy path.
- Provide deterministic sample apps (chat + embedding search) that run with the hosted Redwood Sandbox and with a local sim runner.
- Telemetry opt-in must be explicit, minimal, and reversible.

High-level flow (happy-path):
1) Install: curl | npm | pip quick commands.
2) Run: redwood-starter init  (creates project skeleton, .redwoodrc mock creds)
3) Run local sim: redwood-starter sim up  (spins lightweight process that mimics API latency/limits)
4) Start sample app: npm start / python run_app.py (app points at sim by default)
5) Exercise prompts: guided checklist in terminal that hits generation, streaming, function calling, and embeddings
6) Optional: connect to hosted API (instructions + link to Console)

CLI sketch (happy path commands):
- npm i -g @redwood/starter  OR  pipx install redwood-starter
- redwood-starter init --template=chat-search --name=todo-demo
- cd todo-demo
- redwood-starter sim up --memory=256MB
- yarn start  (or python -m starter.app)
- redwood-starter report  (outputs a short diagnostics + telemetry prompt)

Examples and snippets (should live in the skeleton project):
- example .redwoodrc (local dev)
  REDWOOD_API_KEY=local-sim-key
  REDWOOD_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8083

- sample JS client initialization:
  const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/sdk');
  const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, endpoint: process.env.REDWOOD_ENDPOINT });

- sample Python streaming quickstart:
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'), endpoint=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_ENDPOINT'))
  for chunk in client.generate_stream('Summarize this document in 2 bullets'):
      print(chunk, end='')

Failure modes and recovery (notes for docs + CLI hints):
- Sim fails to start (common: port collision). CLI should detect and suggest alt port and a single-line command to rebind.
- Missing env file: detect, create template, and explain security implications.
- Long token latency in streaming sample: explain batching defaults and point to --low-latency flag that uses small-batch fast-path.
- Rate limit from hosted sandbox: surface clear message with link to Console and suggestion to run sim locally.

Telemetry / privacy model (sketch):
- On first run show interactive prompt: "Help us improve the starter by sending anonymized usage telemetry? Y/n"
- Telemetry payload minimal: command run, OS, SDK version, non-identifying sample of errors (stack hash), duration of command.
- Provide redwood-starter telemetry status: redwood-starter telemetry status  (returns ON/OFF + link to delete data request workflow)
- All telemetry opt-out default for enterprise templates; if user runs --enterprise flag, telemetry is OFF and CLI prints admin contact info.

Local sim behavior and fidelity tradeoffs:
- Sim provides small model runtime behavior deterministically using scripted responses for quick lab checks. Not for quality evaluation.
- Sim supports: streaming shapes, chunking, function call placeholders, embedding distance emulation (simple cosine-based synthetic vectors), and quota enforcement to exercise client retry logic.
- Performance: target < 100ms local response for scripted completions to keep interactions snappy.

Testing and QA checklist (for eng and QA):
- Unit tests for init templates rendering (snapshot tests).
- E2E tests: run init -> sim up -> start app -> hit /health endpoints -> run sample prompts (CI uses headless mode).
- Chaos case test: sim injects delayed chunk to verify client-side progress indicators and reconnect handling.
- Platform gating: must pass security static scan for stored example secrets (no real keys).

Developer docs outline (content to author in docs site):
- Quickstart (2 min) — one-liner install + run + open sample
- Guided tour (10 min) — walkthrough of APIs used by sample app with small code snippets
- Troubleshooting — mapped to CLI exit codes and suggested fixes
- Security & privacy — what the starter stores and how to remove it
- Transitioning to hosted API — steps and Console links to create API key and update .redwoodrc

Measurement and success metrics (proposal):
- Time to first successful generation (goal: median < 5 minutes for new users)
- Completion rate of starter flow (goal: > 65% complete within 15 minutes)
- Demo conversion: % of starter projects that add a hosted key within 7 days (goal: 12%)
- Telemetry opt-in rate and churn feedback (used to prioritize docs pain points)

Open questions / decisions to resolve:
- Should templates include a minimal server (Express/Flask) or purely serverless functions? Pros/cons appended below.
- How opinionated should default client retry/backoff be for the starter? Tradeoffs: predictability vs realism.
- Do we surface a single "low-cost" recommended model for the hosted sandbox, or let template pick?

Template tradeoffs notes (short):
- Server included: easier to demo web UI and sockets for streaming; adds complexity in local env.
- Serverless only: lighter, easier to port to Next/Vercel demos; less clear for raw websocket streaming.

Next actions (short-term backlog):
- Asha: prototype redwood-starter init + sim up (spike) — 1 week
- Liam: draft starter template code for chat-search sample and snapshot tests — 1 week
- Sofia: write quickstart copy and short GIFs for docs — 5 days
- Noah: CI bake for e2e and telemetry opt-out test — 1 week

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the sample prompts short; users paste into Slack or README easily.
- Consider a `redwood-starter export` that bundles a sanitized ZIP for sharing with Sales.
- Avoid embedding real API keys in examples; provide clear one-liner to rotate if user accidentally set production key.

References and links (to include in final doc):
- Confluence: Starter UX patterns (link TBD)
- Jira: DEVEX-1142 (starter wizard feature epic)
- GitHub: repo redwood-sdk-starter (prototype branch: wizard-sim)

End of sketch.

Unresolved: exact CLI UX wording, visual onboarding screens for Console link, and final telemetry retention policy.

\n(End of file - working draft; expect iterative changes and short-run experiments.)
